production.note: US model years 2025 to present. First: PCNA's release for 'The 2025 Porsche 911 models' (deliveries 'at the end of 2024 for the 911 Carrera GTS models'). Still on sale: Renndriver's guide (Joe Armstrong, updated 21 July 2026; renndriver-911-carrera-gts) describes 'The current 992.2 GTS T-Hybrid'. No US page for a 2026 or later model year was opened.

body.note: PCNA: 'in Coupe or Cabriolet form, and as a Targa variant (exclusively available with all-wheel drive)'. The Cabriolet is the open version of this variant; the Targa 4 GTS and Carrera 4 GTS (all-wheel drive) are sold under their own names and are not part of this record.

configuration.note: 'a newly developed 3.6 liter boxer engine'; C/D panel: 'turbocharged and intercooled flat-6'.

displacementL.note: Porsche states '3.6 liter' ('The heart of the T-Hybrid powertrain is a newly developed 3.6 liter boxer engine'); no cc figure was found on an opened page, so the stated litre figure is used.

aspiration.note: One turbocharger: the hybrid system 'allows for the use of a single turbocharger compared to the two that were used previously' (an electrically driven turbocharger).

fuel.note: C/D panel: 'turbocharged and intercooled flat-6, 478 hp, 420 lb-ft + AC motor, 64 hp, 110 lb-ft (combined output: 532 hp, 449 lb-ft; 0.9-kWh lithium-ion battery pack)'. Porsche T-Hybrid; a full hybrid that is not plugged in (inferred from the small battery and Porsche's description).

transmission.note: 'A new, strengthened eight-speed dual-clutch transmission (PDK)'; no manual is offered (Renndriver: 'The current 992.2 GTS T-Hybrid is PDK only'). DCT is Porsche PDK.

powerHp.note: Combined system output. Quote: "The total system power is 398 kW (532 hp) and 449 lb.-ft." C/D panel (cd-2025-911-carrera-gts): "(combined output: 532 hp, 449 lb-ft; ...)". The engine alone makes 478 hp. Renndriver gives 534 hp, a PS conversion (see discrepancies).

weightLb.note: 2025 coupe with the 8-speed PDK (only transmission). Car and Driver road-test curb weight (owner decision 9 October 2026: accepted at weight step 2; it is the measured test car). Quote: "Curb Weight: 3638 lb". Test car optioned (as tested $182,895 vs base $166,895). PCNA gives only the increase ('The U.S. curb weight increase of the new 911 Carrera GTS Coupe compared to the predecessor is a moderate 103 lbs.'), not a figure; no Porsche US curb weight was found.

discrepancies.reason: Renndriver gives 'Total system output is 541 PS, or 534 hp', a conversion of the European PS rating; 532 hp is Porsche's published US rating.
discrepancies.resolution: 532 used: the manufacturer's US rating as published.
